subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — OmniHealth vendor comparison
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lowe <jamie.low@omnihealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — competitive bake-off (Redwood, Spinlytics, CloudServ)

Hi Jamie / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so the team is aligned and we can move forward with a small bake-off:

Pain points & goals
- High token costs with current provider when running batch summarization of medical notes.
- Latency spikes during peak ingestion windows (reports of 800–1,200ms tail latency).
- Need predictable, auditable inference for PHI-sensitive workloads (data residency + audit logs).
- Goal: reduce per-token cost by ~40% while keeping p50 latency under 200ms for user-facing requests and p95 under 600ms for batch processing.

Decision criteria (what OmniHealth told us):
1) Accuracy parity with current model (no >5% degradation on clinical NER/evidence extraction).
2) Cost per 1M tokens (total cost of ownership).
3) Latency SLOs and predictable scaling.
4) Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS integration, VPC/private deployment).

Proposed bake-off scope & tests
- Smoke test: quick interactive generation for 10 representative prompts (functional parity).
- Throughput test: 1-hour batch run simulating 100k tokens/min (observe batching/caching benefits).
- Latency profile: 1k concurrent small requests to measure p50/p95.
- Regression check: run your clinical NER eval suite (we can host the eval or run on your infra—your choice).

Attachments: redwood-vs-competitor-matrix.xlsx (vendor comparison), bakeoff-test-plan.pdf (test cases + metrics)
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-redwood-bakeoff

Next steps / timeline
- We propose a 2-week bake-off window. Suggested kickoff: Mar 22 (live tests) with pre-run on Mar 20 to validate tooling.
- Action items:
  - Jamie: confirm which evals you want included and whether testing can run on your VPC or if you'd prefer Redwood-hosted harness.
  - Priya: share the security contacts for SOC2/KMS questions (we'll include Sean on the thread for technical details).
  - Aditya / Rishi: we'll prepare the test harness + pricing options and send by EOD Mar 17.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if you'd prefer to walk through the matrix.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198
From: Jamie Lowe <jamie.low@omnihealth.com>

Date: 2028-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — competitive bake-off (Redwood, Spinlytics, CloudServ)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap.

A couple quick clarifications before we schedule the tests:
- For the latency SLOs: p50 under 200ms is for the interactive clinician UI only; batch can be higher (we care about cost there).
- Data residency: all patient data must remain in our AWS account (us-east-1). Would prefer Redwood to run the harness against our VPC; can you confirm that's supported for the test? If not, we need an on-prem-looking setup.
- Security contact: looping in our InfoSec lead Priya; she'll own the questionnaire and evidence requests.

Could you confirm whether Redwood's fallback model strategy (in case of capacity) would automatically route to a cheaper quantized variant? That's a potential blocker for accuracy-sensitive evaluations.

We're open to a Mar 22 live run but want the pre-run on Mar 20 as you suggested. Also please add the throughput test details (RPS, payload sizes) to the Drive doc.

Thanks,
Jamie

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — answers + test plan updates

Jamie — quick answers and updates below. I've attached an updated matrix with a column on quantization behavior.

1) Data residency / VPC testing- We can run the test harness against your AWS VPC in us-east-1. Aditya will work with your infra team to set up a short-lived connector (no customer data is stored outside your account during the test). If the team prefers, we can also provide HAR files and a Redwood-hosted dry-run.

2) Fallback/quantization behavior- Redwood's runtime will only fall back to a quantized variant if you opt into that profile for the bake-off. For the accuracy-sensitive evals we recommend locking the model family and disabling automatic fallback. We do support a separate "cost-optimized" lane you can test in parallel. The updated matrix shows expected accuracy impact by quantization profile.

3) Throughput test details (added to Drive):
- Payload: 512-token average per request for batch summarization.
- Target throughput: 100k tokens/min for 1 hour (we'll run ramp-up and steady-state windows).
- Concurrency for latency profile: 1k concurrent 40–60 token requests to simulate clinician UI.

4) Schedule
- Pre-run (tooling validation): Mar 20, 10:00–12:00 PT (no production data)
- Live bake-off: Mar 22, 09:00–13:00 PT

Action items (owners):
- Aditya: set up VPC connector + test harness artifacts, coordinate with OmniHealth infra by Mar 19.
- Rishi: finalize pricing scenarios for locked vs cost-optimized lanes and share by EOD Mar 18.
- Sean: prepare SOC2/KMS brief and be ready to join the security call with Priya.

Attachments: redwood-vs-competitor-matrix.xlsx (updated), bakeoff-test-plan.pdf
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-redwood-bakeoff

If that all looks good I'll send a calendar invite for the pre-run and loop Aditya into OmniHealth's infra channel.

Best,
Marissa

Status & owners:
- VPC connector (Aditya): need Terraform snippet and short-lived creds to hand to OmniHealth infra. Coordinate with Jamie's infra contact (they'll share the AWS role ARN today). Target: complete by EOD Mar 19.
- Pricing proposal (Rishi): prepare two line items — locked accuracy lane and cost-optimized lane; include expected per-token delta and escalation rules. Target: EOD Mar 18 (sent to Jamie/Priya).
- Security brief (Sean): SOC2 scope, KMS integration steps, audit log exports examples. Be ready for a 30-min call with Priya on Mar 21.
- Test harness (Aditya + Marissa): confirm that the harness can run against a VPC connector and produce the same metrics uploaded to our Drive folder.

Notes: Make sure the bakeoff-test-plan.pdf version we attach tomorrow includes explicit success criteria (accuracy delta thresholds + latency budget) so the evaluation is unambiguous. I'll own the calendar invites and external comms.

Thanks — Marissa
